content:
Unrolling the recurrence gives
\[
f(n)=512^{\sum_{i\ge 1}\lfloor n/10^i\rfloor}=512^{S(n)}.
\]
Since \(512=2^9\), the number of hexadecimal digits of \(f(n)\) is
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{9S(n)}{4}\right\rfloor+1.
\]
Thus the condition is
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{9S(n)}{4}\right\rfloor+1\le 2500
\iff S(n)\le 1111.
\]

Now count \(n\) with \(S(n)\le 1111\).

- For \(0\le n\le 9999\), the maximum is
  \[
  S(9999)=999+99+9=1107\le 1111,
  \]
  so all \(10000\) such \(n\) work.

- For a five-digit number \(n=10000+r\), \(0\le r\le 89999\),
  \[
  S(n)=1111+S(r).
  \]
  This is \(\le 1111\) only when \(S(r)=0\), i.e. \(r=0,1,\dots,9\). So there are \(10\) more.

- For \(n\ge 100000\), \(S(n)\ge S(100000)=11111>1111\), so none work.

Therefore the total number is
\[
10000+10=10010.
\]

\[
\boxed{10010}
\]
